title: Arm and leg dominant UL
author: Adam W.
desc:
Higher intensity program with an emphasis on arm and leg musculature.  All muscles are trained with very high RPE, only the volume is turned up for arms and legs.

Note on progression: Once you have reached the top end of the range, increase the weight for that set. This means you should not be increasing your weight for all sets at the same time in most cases.

ex.note: These can be performed before preachers if preferred.
Neutral or prone grip are both fine.
Lower the bar to your nose or forehead with no shoulder movement. I placed this after pushdowns to allow to elbows to be more warmed up, as this exercise is often more stressful.
Aim for 8 to 12 full reps and then perform partials until complete muscular failure. I prefer seated on a 75 degree incline.
Drop the incline to 15 or 30 degrees and perform lying face down. Go until complete muscular failure.
For sets 2 and 3 perform forced reps until you meet set one rep count. Ex. If you got 12 reps on set one but only 10 on set two you will perform 2 forced reps using minimal upper body assistance.
You can superset the seated and standing but I advise only resting 10 to 15 seconds between each set anyway.
Supersets are optional. If they take away from the intensity you can put into each movement, I would adivse against them.
Perform immediately after finishing second set of OHP. Second set is a drop set.
Start from the top and lower your arms to 90 degrees pausing at peak tension. Keep your grip close, pinning your elbows to your sides.
Keep the weight the same for all sets but anticipate a major drop-off in rep count. All sets should be performed until even minor partial reps become very difficult.
These can be performed before preachers if preferred.
